title: Wrap a long line with continuations

blocks.text: The page's best practice for a very long single-line string is the line continuation escape: a `\` at the end of a text block line suppresses the line break, so the source reads well and the value stays one line. Its example:
Write `LongLine.source(String sentence, int width)`. `sentence` is words separated by single spaces (no quote, no backslash, no leading or trailing space). Return the text block source for it:

items: the sentence split into pieces, filled greedily: each piece takes as many whole words as fit in `width` characters, a word longer than `width` takes a piece of its own and is **never cut**;
the space where the sentence breaks stays at the end of the piece before it, and **counts** towards its width (a piece of exactly `width` characters fits);
each piece indented by eight spaces; every piece but the last ends with `\` and `\n`, the last ends with the closing `"""`.

cases.says: The sentence is split after spaces into source lines that end with \, each keeping the space it breaks at, and the last line ends with the closing delimiter.
A source line whose text is exactly width characters long still fits.
The space kept at the end of a piece counts towards its width.
A word longer than the width gets a line of its own and is never cut.

concepts: Line continuation writes a very long single-line value across several readable source lines.
